hints: Apply the remainder theorem at the zeros of the divisors: use $f(-2a)=-22a^3$ and $f(a/3)=-a^3$.
Substitute carefully into every power of $x$, then divide each equation by $a^3$, which is non-zero.
Simplify to two linear equations in $p$ and $q$, solve them simultaneously, and check both stated remainders.
walkthrough:
Apply the remainder theorem with the divisor $(3x - a)$: $f\left(\dfrac{a}{3}\right) = -a^3$:
$$f\left(\dfrac{a}{3}\right) = 3\left(\dfrac{a}{3}\right)^3 + pa\left(\dfrac{a}{3}\right)^2 + 7a^2\left(\dfrac{a}{3}\right) + qa^3 = -a^3$$
$$3\left(\dfrac{a^3}{27}\right) + pa\left(\dfrac{a^2}{9}\right) + \dfrac{7}{3}a^3 + qa^3 = -a^3$$
$$\dfrac{1}{9}a^3 + \dfrac{p}{9}a^3 + \dfrac{7}{3}a^3 + qa^3 = -a^3$$
$$\text{Divide by } a^3: \quad \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{p}{9} + \dfrac{7}{3} + q = -1$$

Clear denominators by multiplying by $9$:
$$1 + p + 9\left(\dfrac{7}{3}\right) + 9q = 9(-1)$$
$$1 + p + 21 + 9q = -9$$
$$p + 9q + 22 = -9$$
$$p + 9q = -9 - 22 \implies p + 9q = -31 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Solve equations (1) and (2) simultaneously for $p$ and $q$:
$$\text{From (1): } q = 16 - 4p$$
$$\text{Substitute into (2): } p + 9(16 - 4p) = -31$$
$$p + 144 - 36p = -31$$
$$-35p = -31 - 144 = -175$$
$$p = \dfrac{-175}{-35} = 5$$
